newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Tengelmann subsidiary opens Hungary's largest store.
newsitem.headline: Tengelmann subsidiary opens Hungary's largest store.

text.p: Hungarian department store chain Skala-Coop, majority owned by Germany's Tengelmann retail group, opened the country's largest department store in Budapest on Thursday.
Skala's managing director Janos Halasz told reporters the 8,000 square metre store represents an investment of one billion forints ($160 million).
The development coincides with the unveiling of Hungary's first two U.S.-style shopping malls, both also sited in the capital.
The first, the $55 million Duna Plaza, was opened earlier this month by a consortium of the Hungarian Foreign Trade Bank, Israeli Bank Hapoalim and the Hungarian Transelektro Plaza Kft.
The $120 million Polus Centre, will open on November 8 and was built by Granit Polus Rt, jointly owned by a group of North American investors and U.S. real estate development firm Trisec.
Skala-Coop Series T shares closed 20 down on Thursday at 1,540 forints.
